question: On a new published Karel program, can a fixed rule or a ranker trained on other programs select a demonstrated primitive-action plan that reaches the target endpoint on the observed initial world?
data_gate: Use the same first 2500 records (or all if fewer) and first six worlds as the Karel trace control. Require exact own-world replay, all 1000 author code strings present in the pinned mirror, and a validated archive hash. Report whether author order matches. The corroboration covers code strings, not every world or demonstration. No new dataset download. Do not silently discard records or failing predictions.
unit: For each program, leave each world out and use up to the other five as support. Require at least two worlds. Coalesce identical demonstrated action sequences into a candidate with a known support count. Empty plan means immediate STOP and participates normally.
allowed: Program identity is available only to group the splits. Every selector sees support input worlds and observed support actions plus the complete target input world. Simulate known deterministic primitives to evaluate legality and observable predicates. No target program text, target actions, or target output may enter candidate features or inference. Only supervised training-fold labels and post-selection scoring use the target endpoint.
signature: At the initial boundary and after every successful action through the terminal STOP boundary, record four booleans: front clear, left clear, right clear and marker present. On a legal target replay, compare its signature to each donor for that candidate; similarity is mean matched bits divided by four over all boundaries. Use the best donor similarity. If target replay crashes, assign similarity zero. A zero-action plan has one boundary.

methods.mode: Largest multiplicity of candidate among supports.
methods.legality_mode: Choose lexicographically by legal replay and then support count. If all candidates crash, choose by count.
methods.sensor: Choose lexicographically by legal replay, best predicate similarity, then support count.
methods.ranker: Group exact whitespace-normalized published program token streams by SHA256 using a fixed salt and mod 5. Fit each fold using only the other four folds. An unweighted-bias logistic regression with features (legal, support frequency, best predicate similarity) and unpenalized intercept, L2 penalty 0.01 on the three coefficients, predicts exact endpoint replay success. Each program contributes unit total weight, each target equal within program, each unique candidate equal within target. Fixed Newton updates to convergence or 40 iterations, no tuning. Use maximum predicted success.
methods.oracle: Best endpoint success attainable among the same candidates; a retrospective ceiling.

scoring: Average exactly over candidates tied in score (absolute tolerance 1e-12 for numeric scores), then targets equally within program, then eligible program records equally. Report absolute endpoint success for all methods, paired gain of ranker over legality_mode and sensor with descriptive 95% percentile bootstrap using 2000 resamples of whole exact-program groups, fixed seed 20261120. Report number of records, canonical programs, folds and candidate replays, primitive-step attempts and distinct support and target simulations. If a fold is empty or train/test overlap by canonical code, stop. Report coverage when a legal support candidate matches all four predicates at every boundary including STOP, its exact-trace and endpoint reliability, and any violations. No semantic certificate claim if observable set is incomplete.
decision: Retain a learned-selector candidate for further study only if ranker gains at least one percentage point over both frozen outcome-blind baselines (legality_mode and sensor) and both lower paired interval endpoints exceed zero. Other results may quantify the limits or strength of simple prospective selection. A single Karel validation bank and complete initial target map cannot distinguish online necessity, meta-control or general transfer to novel skill sets. Known-simulator calls have cost.
resources: One free school CPU allocation, at most five minutes, no GPU or local model. Only after the primary Karel reference replay gate passes.
